issues.body:
WEB_RDF_ACCEPT (import-drawer.tsx:103-107) is now passed verbatim to pickTextFiles({accept}) from handleBrowse (import-drawer.tsx:723-728), which forwards it into showOpenFilePicker's options.types[].accept (file-ingest.ts:184-192). The File System Access 'verify a suffix' algorithm rejects any suffix containing a code point outside ASCII alphanumeric, '+' and '.'; '.json-ld' contains a hyphen. I have no network here to run a live browser check, so I state this as a concrete risk rather than a confirmed break.

The failure mode is what makes it worth blocking: pickTextFiles catches every non-AbortError and falls back to pickViaInput (file-ingest.ts:205-208). If the suffix IS rejected, every 'Browse files…' click quietly takes the hidden-input path and the PR's stated goal — 'retain the File System Access API path where available' (import-drawer.tsx:721-722) — is false in the only browser family that ships FSA, with no error surfaced anywhere. The library's own doc comment at file-ingest.ts:168-172 already lists 'option TypeError' as an anticipated failure, which is evidence this is a live hazard.

Note the list does double duty: it is both the ingest filter (where '.json-ld' is genuinely useful, since FORMAT_OPTIONS at rdf-format.ts:23 maps 'json-ld' to jsonld) and the picker dialog filter (where it may be illegal). Those two consumers need different treatment. Unchanged since round 3.
issues.fix_hint:
Verify first — in a Chrome console run showOpenFilePicker({types:[{description:'x',accept:{'text/plain':['.json-ld']}}]}) and observe whether it throws TypeError before the dialog opens.

Either way, harden the library rather than only the caller: in pickTextFiles, filter opts.accept down to picker-legal suffixes before building `types` (drop any suffix not matching /^\.[a-z0-9+.]{1,16}$/i after lowercasing), and keep the FULL list for the readFiles extension check so ingest behaviour is unchanged. That keeps '.json-ld' working as an ingest filter, keeps the dialog filter valid, and makes the library robust for future consumers. Optionally distinguish a genuine option TypeError from a SecurityError in the catch at file-ingest.ts:205 so a misconfigured accept list is not indistinguishable from an unsupported browser.
issues.title: '.json-ld' in WEB_RDF_ACCEPT likely makes showOpenFilePicker throw TypeError, silently killing the FSA path this PR exists to restore

issues.body:
The point of adding `readFile` to IngestOptions is that a consumer no longer needs its own copy of the ingest loop. handleBrowse now uses it, but handleDrop (import-drawer.tsx:688-718) still duplicates readDroppedFiles verbatim — the items/kind loop, the webkitGetAsEntry directory check, the getAsFile null check, and both reason strings are copy-pasted from file-ingest.ts:227-252 — and readFilesWithDecompress (import-drawer.tsx:600-622) now duplicates readFiles (file-ingest.ts:100-121) almost line for line, including the newly added 'could not be read: ' prefix.

Most concretely, import-drawer.tsx:607 inlines `unsupported file type — expected ${WEB_RDF_ACCEPT.join(" / ")}` instead of calling the library's rejectedReasonUnsupported (file-ingest.ts:91-93). The two are byte-identical today, so the drop and browse paths agree — but nothing enforces that, and the moment the library message is reworded the same rejected file reports different text depending on how it entered. The duplicated 'could not be read: ' prefix at import-drawer.tsx:617 vs file-ingest.ts:117 has the same hazard, and the new test at file-ingest.test.ts:57-59 pins the library copy only. Unchanged since round 3.
issues.title: Refactor is half-landed: handleDrop still hand-rolls readDroppedFiles, and duplicates the reject-reason string

issues.body:
The tests are non-vacuous: test 1 proves the custom reader is used AND that the default File.text() is not (the defaultReaderCalled === false assertion is the real mutation guard), test 2 pins the 'could not be read: ' prefix, test 3 proves the accept filter short-circuits before the reader runs. The fakes are sound — droppedFile() sets items:[] so `dataTransfer.items?.length` is falsy and the FileList branch at file-ingest.ts:249-252 is taken, which is a real path. Wiring into package.json test:unit is correct.

But all three go through readDroppedFiles, and import-drawer.tsx does NOT call readDroppedFiles — it hand-rolls the drop path (previous finding). The only new production consumer of `readFile` is pickTextFiles via handleBrowse (import-drawer.tsx:723-728), and that has no coverage; neither does the new accept-filter branch in readFilesWithDecompress (import-drawer.tsx:604-610), which is not exported and so not testable at all. Coverage is real because readFiles is shared by both entry points, so this is mis-aimed rather than fake — but as written the suite would stay green if handleBrowse's readFile option were dropped entirely. Unchanged since round 3.

(Note: I could not execute the suite here — `node --import ./test-support/register-ts.mjs` fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for 'typescript' because node_modules is absent; the pre-existing file-decompress.test.ts fails identically, so this is environmental.)
issues.fix_hint: Add a pickTextFiles case covering the option that actually changed. It is testable in Node without a DOM: stub globalThis.window with a showOpenFilePicker returning a fake handle whose getFile() resolves the fake File, stub globalThis.document, then assert the custom readFile ran and the default File.text() did not — mirroring test 1. Add one case asserting a handle whose getFile() rejects lands in `rejected` with the 'could not be read: ' prefix (file-ingest.ts:196-202), currently uncovered. A case asserting an accept list containing '.json-ld' still produces a working picker call would also pin the major finding above. If handleDrop is collapsed onto readDroppedFiles, the existing three tests then cover the drop path for real.
issues.title: New tests exercise readDroppedFiles, which the import drawer does not call — the changed production path is untested

issues.body:
Before this PR the drop/input path applied no extension filter — every file went straight to maybeDecompressFile, and guessFormat's fallback (rdf-format.ts:62) parsed unknown extensions as turtle. The new check at import-drawer.tsx:604 rejects anything outside the 15-entry list, so files that previously imported successfully — .n3, .rdf, .owl, and any RDF file with a non-standard or absent extension — now fail with 'unsupported file type'. Tightening is defensible and probably intended, but it is a user-visible behaviour change that neither the PR description nor gui/README.md records.

The sharper problem is .hdt. The pane copy at import-drawer.tsx:741-743 prominently promises 'Native-only HDT archives (.hdt) still require the desktop app', and guessFormat/isHdt (rdf-format.ts:47-50, 58) have dedicated HDT handling. But .hdt is not in WEB_RDF_ACCEPT, so a dropped .hdt now produces the generic 'unsupported file type — expected .ttl / .turtle / …' — the one case where the UI has already told the user a specific, actionable answer, and the filter throws it away. (A .hdt.gz slips through the filter on the .gz suffix and is then handed to importRdf with format 'hdt' at import-drawer.tsx:271, a separate inconsistency.) Unchanged since round 3.
issues.title: New drop-path accept filter rejects files that previously imported, and gives .hdt a message contradicting the pane's own copy

issues.body:
maybeDecompressFile returns MaybeDecompressedFile with an `effectiveName` field that exists precisely so the caller can detect format from the INNER name (file-decompress.ts:22-27, 104, 122-123). decompressReader (import-drawer.tsx:597-598) throws it away and returns only `.text`, because IngestOptions.readFile is typed `(file: File) => Promise<string>` (file-ingest.ts:60).

Downstream, format is chosen by guessFormat(file.name) at import-drawer.tsx:271 — the OUTER name. That recovers correctly for .gz/.bz2/.zst/.zstd only, because COMPRESSION_EXTS (rdf-format.ts:28) contains exactly those four. But WEB_RDF_ACCEPT also admits .zip, .tgz, .gzip and .bzip2, none of which stripCompression strips. So `data.nq.zip` yields ext 'zip', no FORMAT_OPTIONS hit, and the turtle fallback — an N-Quads or JSON-LD payload handed to the turtle parser.

This is pre-existing (the old readFilesWithDecompress discarded decoded.effectiveName the same way) and is NOT a regression, so it is not a blocker. I raise it because this PR is the one that fixes the shape of the reader contract into the shared library, and the string-only signature makes the bug unfixable at the library level for every future consumer. Unchanged since round 3.
issues.fix_hint:
Widen the hook now while it has exactly one caller:

  readFile?: (file: File) => Promise<string | { text: string; effectiveName?: string }>

and in readFiles (file-ingest.ts:113-114) push `name: result.effectiveName ?? file.name` when the object form comes back. Then decompressReader can return the whole MaybeDecompressedFile and `data.nq.zip` is imported as nquads. Adding 'zip'/'tgz'/'gzip'/'bzip2' to COMPRESSION_EXTS is the wrong alternative — stripping '.zip' from 'archive.zip' leaves no inner extension at all. Fine to land as a follow-up bead if the signature is widened now.
issues.title: readFile's string-only return type discards effectiveName, so zip/tgz archives get the wrong RDF format

issues.body:
pickViaInput resolves only on 'change' or 'cancel' (file-ingest.ts:153-160). The 'cancel' event on <input type="file"> is relatively recent; on engines that do not fire it, a user who opens the dialog and dismisses it leaves the promise pending forever, and the hidden input has already been appended to document.body (file-ingest.ts:148).

Previously handleBrowse just called inputRef.current.click() and returned synchronously, so this could not happen on this path. It is harmless in practice — handleBrowse sets no busy flag, so nothing locks up and the button stays usable — which is why this is a nit. The cost is a small leak (a detached-but-appended input plus a retained closure) per dismissed dialog. Unchanged since round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Nothing required for this PR. If you want to close it in the library, add a one-shot window 'focus' listener alongside the 'cancel' listener in pickViaInput: on focus return, defer a tick and, if no 'change' has fired, resolve emptyResult() and remove the input. That is the standard workaround and preserves the no-silent-drop invariant, since a cancel legitimately means nothing was selected.
issues.title: handleBrowse now awaits a promise that can never settle when the browser does not fire the input 'cancel' event

issues.body:
Three staleness points, all unchanged since round 3:

1. gui/README.md gives readFile a mid-clause parenthetical. It is a public API addition to IngestOptions and deserves its own sentence in the 'Entry points' paragraph — noting the default is File.text() and that the Import drawer overrides it with maybeDecompressFile — since it is what makes binary consumers possible at all.

2. The JSDoc block at import-drawer.tsx:590-596 was written for readFilesWithDecompress, but `decompressReader` is now inserted between the comment and the function (import-drawer.tsx:597-598), so the comment binds to the const in IDEs/TypeDoc. Its text is also stale: it says the helper 'Replaces the readDroppedFiles / File.text() call paths in the web-upload pane', but the browse path now goes through pickTextFiles, not this helper.

3. The drop-zone hint at import-drawer.tsx:776-778 still lists '.ttl · .nt · .nq · .trig · .jsonld · .gz · .zip · .zst · .bz2' and was not updated for the newly accepted .turtle / .ntriples / .nquads / .json-ld aliases. Users now get 'unsupported file type' listing 15 extensions while the visible hint advertises 9 — the filter and the hint disagree in both directions.
issues.fix_hint: Derive the hint text from WEB_RDF_ACCEPT (e.g. WEB_RDF_ACCEPT.join(' · ')) so it cannot drift. Move the JSDoc block below `decompressReader` so it attaches to readFilesWithDecompress, and reword it to say the helper serves the input and drop paths while the browse path uses pickTextFiles with the same decompressReader. In gui/README.md, give readFile its own sentence in the Entry points paragraph.
issues.title: Doc drift: drop-zone hint lists 9 extensions where the filter admits 15, and the helper JSDoc now attaches to the wrong symbol

verdict.summary:
Round 4 is materially identical to round 3: the head is still `fix: address review round 1 for #4062`, and every line the prior round cited (import-drawer.tsx:604-610, 720-731, 776-778; WEB_RDF_ACCEPT; file-ingest.ts:113) is unchanged. No round-3 finding was addressed — hence stagnant, and the same concerns stand at the same severities.

Directionally right: the optional `readFile` hook (file-ingest.ts:57-60, 113) lets handleBrowse keep the File System Access path while still decompressing archives; the widened aliases line up exactly with FORMAT_OPTIONS (rdf-format.ts:19-23); the accept filter upholds no-silent-drop; the test file is wired into `test:unit`. The tests are non-vacuous — test 1's `defaultReaderCalled === false` is a real mutation guard. I could not execute them (no node_modules; the pre-existing file-decompress.test.ts fails identically), so I verified by tracing readFiles/readDroppedFiles.

The blocking concern remains that this PR may disable the path it exists to restore: showOpenFilePicker validates every suffix in options.types[].accept against ASCII alphanumeric + '+' + '.', and the newly added '.json-ld' contains a hyphen. pickTextFiles swallows that TypeError into the hidden-input fallback (file-ingest.ts:205-208), so the FSA path would silently die in the only browser family that ships it, with zero signal — and the library's own doc comment already names 'option TypeError' as an expected failure.

Secondary gaps, all unchanged: the refactor is half-landed (handleDrop and readFilesWithDecompress still hand-roll readDroppedFiles/readFiles, duplicating two reason literals); the tests aim at a path the drawer does not call; the drop filter regresses previously-importable files and gives .hdt a message contradicting the pane's own copy; readFile's string return discards effectiveName.

No security issues: reject reasons render as escaped React text; no reviewer-directed text in the diff.
